newsitem.title: USA: Central Illinois power units seen back by Monday.
newsitem.headline: Central Illinois power units seen back by Monday.

text.p: Central Illinois Light Co said it expected to be back at full electrical generation capacity by Monday, Nov 11, after taking several units off line for maintenance, a company spokeswoman said Wednesday.

The company's 366 megawatt (MW) Duck Creek coal-fired power plant in near Canton, Ill. was taken off line late Tuesday for repairs, and was expected to resume production on Thursday, said company spokeswoman Marybeth Williams.
When the Duck Creek plant returns to service, the 117 MW unit 1 at the Edwards coal-fired plant just south of Peoria, Ill., will be shut through to the weekend for repairs, Williams said.
Edwards unit 1 is expected to return to service over the weekend, when the 361 MW Edwards unit 3 will then be taken out of service for a short period, also for repairs.
The Edwards station is made up of three units with a total generation capacity of 740 MW.
"By Monday we should be back to normal generation," Williams said.
Both Duck Creek and Edwards are fully owned and operated by Central Illinois Light.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
